Petition under Section 166 & 140 of M.V. Act, 1988 for grant of compensation Award
1.

The petitioners have filed the present claim petition U/s 166/140 M.V Act, seeking compensation to the tune of Rs. 50,00,000/- from the date of accident till its realization for the fatal injury sustained by Shashi Devi, MACP No. 298/23; FIR No. 60/23 DOD:23.12.2025 aged about 46 years in Motor Vehicular Accident which occurred on 17.02.2023 at about 11:48 PM at Yamuna Expressway, Noida, involving Truck bearing registration no. HR55U-0571(offending vehicle) which was being driven by its driver/respondent no.1 in a rash and negligent manner.

2. The concise material facts relevant to decide the present claim are that on 17.02.2023, deceased Shashi Devi alongwith her husband and son was going from Delhi to their ancestral home at Unnao by car bearing registration no. DL3C-AL-5187.
At about 11:48 pm, when they reached at Yamuna Expressway, Noida, the aforesaid car got punctured and her husband stopped the car at the correct side of the road.

In the meantime, when the husband of deceased was busy in making the call to Helpline number, a truck bearing registration no. HR55U-0571 which was being driven by its driver at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, without blowing any horn came from back side and hit the aforesaid car with a great force and dragged the same for about 500 meter, as a result of which, Smt. Shashi Devi Sustained grievous injuries.
She was immediately taken to District Hospital, Mathura, where doctors declared her "Brought Dead".
Her postmortem was conducted at District Mortuary, Mathura, Uttar Pradesh.

A case U/s 279/338/304A IPC was registered at PS.
Raya, District Mathura, UP vide FIR No. 60/23 with regard to the accident in question.

The petitioners have claimed that the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of aforementioned offending Truck which was allegedly being driven by MACP No. 298/23; FIR No.
60/23 DOD:23.12.2025 respondent no.1/driver.
The offending vehicle was found to be owned by respondent no. 2 and was insured with respondent no. 3 at the time of accident in question.

sentences.text: In their separate but similar written statement, the respondent no. 1 & 2 claimed that on the date and time of accident, there was heavy fog and low visibility.

It is further claimed that when respondent no. 1 reached at Yamuna Expressway, suddenly a car bearing registration no.

the accident had taken place and the aforesaid car got struck from front side.
They further claimed that the alleged accident had occurred due to the negligence of driver of the aforesaid car.
They also claimed that respondent no. 1 was having valid driving licence at the time of accident.

They further claimed that offending vehicle was insured with respondent no. 3 at the time of accident and thus,
they are not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners.
On merits, they denied the averments made in the claim petition and prayed for its dismissal.
4. In its written statement, the respondent no. 3 raised preliminary objections that respondent no. 1 was driving the offending vehicle without driving licence.
It is further claimed that alleged accident occurred due to the negligence of driver of car of deceased as he had wrongly parked the car on the Yamuna Expressway.

However, it is admitted that offending vehicle was MACP No. 298/23; FIR No.
60/23 DOD:23.12.2025 insured with it at the time of accident.
On merits, it has denied the averments made in the claim petition and prayed for its dismissal.

5. From the pleadings of the parties and the documents, following issues were framed vide order dated 10.01.2024:-

The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.?OPP.

10. It is evident from the testimony of PW1 that the respondents could not impeach his testimony through litmus test of cross-examination despite the fact that he being cross-examined at length and said witness is found to have successfully withstood the test of cross-examination.

Moreover, it is an undisputed fact that FIR No. 60/23 u/s 279/338/304A IPC was registered at PS. Raya, Mathura,
with regard to accident in question.

Copy of said FIR (Ex. PW1/7), would show that same was registered on the date of accident itself i.e., 17.02.2023 on the basis of statement of aforesaid MACP No. 298/23; FIR No. 60/23 DOD:23.12.2025 witness PW1 Sh. Rajesh Dixit who specifically told the registration number of offending vehicle as HR55U-0571 in his statement.
Thus, FIR is shown to have been registered promptly and without any delay.
Hence, there is no possibility of false implication of respondent no. 1 and/or false involvement of offending vehicle at the instance of petitioners herein.

Moreover, the presence of PW1 at the spot of accident at the time of accident is substantiated by the fact that he joined the investigation with IO and gave statement as a witness and by seeing the list of witnesses annexed alongwith the chargesheet filed in the criminal case shows his name mentioned at S.No.
1.
On the other hand, respondents have not examined any witness in order to rebut the testimony of PW1 in this regard during the course of inquiry.
Hence, there is no reason to disbelieve his uncontroverted testimony on the point of accident in question being caused by respondent no. 1 while driving the offending vehicle.
The contents of said FIR would show that the complainant has disclosed therein the same sequence of facts leading to the accident as deposed by him as PW1 in his evidence.
Hence, there is no possibility of any false implication of driver of offending vehicle or false involvement of the said vehicle in this case.

11. It is pertinent to note that the respondent no.1/driver of offending vehicle was the other material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances, the accident has taken place.
However, he has preferred not to enter into the witness box.

Thus, an adverse inference is MACP No. 298/23; FIR No. 60/23 DOD:23.12.2025 liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the respondent no.1.

sentences.text: In the said case, Hon'ble Apex Court had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.

In Manjuri Bera (supra), the Court observed as under:-
"9.

In terms of clause (c) of subsection (1) of Section 166 of the Act in case of death,
all or any of the legal representatives of the deceased become entitled to compensation and any such legal representative can file a claim petition.

The proviso to said subsection makes the position clear that where all the legal representatives had not joined, then application can be made on behalf of the legal representatives of the deceased by impleading those legal representatives as respondents.
Therefore, the High Court was justified in its view that the appellant could maintain a claim petition in terms of Section 166 of the Act.
10. The Tribunal has a duty to make an award, determine the amount of compensation which is just and proper and specify the person or persons to whom such compensation would be paid.
The latter part relates to the entitlement of compensation by a person who claims for the same.
